name_en: Nonemptiness requirement in the definition of a subspace
name_zh: 子空间定义中的非空性要求
statement: A subspace is defined only for a nonempty subset S of V. Nonemptiness is a separate condition from closure: it is what later supplies a witness element x from which the zero element and negatives are manufactured.

anchors.quote: Given a linear space V, let S be a nonempty subset of V.

atomic_reason: A single quantifier-level condition (S has at least one element). Splitting further would leave no mathematical content.

name_en: A subspace carries the same addition and scalar multiplication as V
name_zh: 子空间沿用母空间的加法与数乘
statement: S must be a linear space under the operations it inherits from V, not under some freshly invented pair of operations. This clause is what makes a subspace a structural part of V rather than an unrelated space that happens to sit inside it as a set.

anchors.quote: If S is also a linear space, with the same operations of addition and multiplication by scalars, then S is called a subspace of V.

atomic_reason: One indivisible stipulation about which operations are used; it has no independently variable parts.

name_en: A subspace satisfies every linear space axiom
name_zh: 子空间满足全部线性空间公理
statement: By definition a subspace is itself a linear space, so all ten axioms hold in S. This is the burden that Theorem 15.4 later reduces to the two closure axioms alone.

anchors.quote: If S is a subspace, it satisfies all the axioms for a linear space

atomic_reason: A pointer to the already-atomized axiom list of 15.02; further splitting duplicates apostol:axioms-for-addition and apostol:axioms-for-multiplication-by-numbers.

name_en: Theorem 15.4 hypothesis: S is a nonempty subset of V
name_zh: 定理15.4的前提:S 是 V 的非空子集
statement: The closure test is asserted only for nonempty S. The hypothesis is not decoration: the empty set satisfies both closure axioms vacuously yet has no zero element, so it is not a subspace.

anchors.quote: Let S be a nonempty subset of a linear space V.

atomic_reason: A single hypothesis clause with one quantifier; nothing inside it varies independently.

name_en: Theorem 15.4, substantive direction: closure implies all remaining axioms
name_zh: 定理15.4的充分性方向:封闭性推出其余公理
statement: The content of Theorem 15.4 is that closure alone forces the other eight axioms in S. The proof splits the eight into two groups: those inherited free from V, and Axioms 5 and 6 which must be constructed.

anchors.quote: Now we show that if S satisfies the closure axioms it satisfies the others as well.

atomic_reason: Not atomic: it decomposes into the inheritance argument and the two explicit constructions of O and of negatives.

name_en: Axioms 3, 4 and 7 through 10 are inherited because they are identities holding for all of V
name_zh: 公理3、4与7至10因对 V 的全部元素成立而自动继承
statement: The commutative and associative laws and the four scalar multiplication axioms are universally quantified identities. Any subset automatically satisfies them, so no property of S is used here beyond S being a subset of V.

anchors.quote: laws for addition (Axioms 3 and 4) and the axioms for multiplication by scalars (Axioms 7 through 10) are automatically satisfied in S because they hold for all elements of V.

atomic_reason: One logical observation (universal identities restrict to subsets); it applies uniformly to the six axioms and does not split per axiom.

name_en: Only Axioms 5 and 6 remain to be verified inside S
name_zh: 只剩公理5与6需在 S 内验证
statement: Existence statements do not restrict to subsets, so the existence of a zero element in S and of a negative for each element of S are the only two obligations left. This is the exact point where the proof needs real work.

anchors.quote: It remains to verify Axioms 5 and 6, the existence of a zero element in S, and the existence of a negative for each element in S.

atomic_reason: A bookkeeping step naming exactly two remaining goals; its two goals are themselves separate nodes below.

name_en: Nonemptiness supplies the witness element x used to build O and negatives
name_zh: 非空性提供了用来造出零元与负元的见证元 x
statement: Both constructions below start from a fixed element x of S, and the only justification for having one is that S is nonempty. This is the single load-bearing use of the nonemptiness hypothesis in the whole proof.

anchors.quote: Let $x$ be any element of $S$ . (S has at least one element since $S$ is not empty.)

atomic_reason: A single existential instantiation step; there is nothing smaller to extract.

name_en: Axiom 2 (closure under scalar multiplication) is the axiom actually applied
name_zh: 真正被使用的是公理2(数乘封闭)
statement: Both constructions run through Axiom 2 with specific scalars, applied to the single witness x. Closure under addition (Axiom 1) is never invoked in the proof of the sufficiency direction.

anchors.quote: By Axiom 2, $ax$ is in $S$ for every scalar $a$ .

atomic_reason: Identifies one axiom application; further decomposition would only restate the axiom itself, which already exists as apostol:closure-axioms.
origin_note: The second sentence (Axiom 1 is never invoked in the sufficiency direction) is a model inference from reading the proof, not a claim Apostol makes; the anchor supports only the first sentence.

name_en: Taking a = 0 puts the zero element into S
name_zh: 取 a = 0 把零元放进 S
statement: Closure under scalar multiplication with a = 0 gives 0x in S, and Theorem 15.3(a) identifies 0x with the zero element O. Hence Axiom 5 holds in S.

anchors.quote: Taking $a = 0$ , it follows that $0x$ is in $S$ . But $0x = O$ , by Theorem 15.3(a), so $O \in S$ , and Axiom 5 is satisfied.

atomic_reason: One instantiation plus one citation of an already existing theorem node; no further independent mathematical content.

name_en: Taking a = -1 puts the negative of x into S
name_zh: 取 a = -1 把 x 的负元放进 S
statement: Closure with a = -1 gives (-1)x in S, and the identity x + (-1)x = O, which holds already in V, shows (-1)x is a negative of x. Hence Axiom 6 holds in S.

anchors.quote: Taking $a = -1$ , we see that $(-1)x$ is in $S$ . But $x + (-1)x = O$ since both $x$ and $(-1)x$ are in $V$ , so Axiom 6 is satisfied in $S$ .

atomic_reason: One instantiation plus one identity imported from V; nothing smaller carries mathematical content.

name_en: Finiteness of the number of terms in a linear combination
name_zh: 线性组合中项数的有限性
statement: A linear combination is a sum over indices 1 through k for some finite k. Only finitely many terms are allowed because a bare linear space has addition of two elements and no notion of convergence, so an infinite sum is undefined.
atomic_reason: A single quantifier-level condition on the index set; removing it does not leave a smaller condition, it destroys the definition.

name_en: The elements combined must lie in S
name_zh: 被组合的元素必须取自 S
statement: The x_i are required to be elements of S, while the combination x itself lives in the ambient V. This asymmetry is what makes the span a construction on S rather than a property of S.

anchors.quote: where $x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}$ are all in S and $c_{1},\ldots,c_{k}$ are scalars, is called a finite linear combination of elements of S.

atomic_reason: One membership condition on the summands; nothing inside varies independently.

name_en: The coefficients range over all scalars, with no constraint
name_zh: 系数取遍全部标量,无任何限制
statement: In the definition of a linear combination the c_i are unrestricted scalars; in particular they may all be zero. The contrast with the dependence definition, which forbids all-zero coefficients, is exactly one clause wide.

anchors.quote: $c_{1},\ldots,c_{k}$ are scalars, is called a finite linear combination of elements of S

atomic_reason: A single absence-of-constraint clause on the coefficient tuple.

name_en: The span is a subspace because it passes the closure test
name_zh: 张成集通过封闭性判别故为子空间
statement: That L(S) is a subspace is not asserted directly: the text checks the closure axioms and then invokes Theorem 15.4. So the very first application of Theorem 15.4 in the book is to the span.

anchors.quote: satisfies the closure axioms and hence is a subspace of V. We call this the subspace spanned by S, or the linear span of S

atomic_reason: One inference chaining a closure check to an existing theorem node; no internal steps remain.

name_en: Convention: the span of the empty set is the zero subspace
name_zh: 约定:空集的张成集为零子空间
statement: For S empty there are no elements to combine, so L(S) is fixed by a separate stipulation to be the one-element set containing only O. Without this convention L(S) would be empty and would fail to be a subspace.

anchors.quote: If S is empty, we define $L(S)$ to be $\{O\}$ , the set consisting of the zero element alone.

atomic_reason: A boundary-case definition covering exactly one input; it cannot be subdivided.

name_en: A subspace does not determine its spanning set
name_zh: 子空间并不决定其张成集
statement: Distinct sets can have the same span; the text exhibits three different sets all spanning V_2, and three different sets all spanning the polynomials of degree at most n. So spanning is a many-to-one relation from sets to subspaces.

anchors.quote: Different sets may span the same subspace. For example, the space $V_{2}$ is spanned by each of the following sets of vectors:

atomic_reason: One non-uniqueness observation, established by the exhibited examples; no smaller claim inside.

name_en: A spanning set may be redundant
name_zh: 张成集可以是冗余的
statement: The set containing O, i, -i, j, -j and i+j spans V_2 while containing the zero element and repeated directions. Spanning therefore imposes no independence requirement, which is precisely why a basis needs a second clause.
atomic_reason: A single independence-free observation about spanning; it is the minimal statement separating spanning from basis.

name_en: A spanning set may be infinite
name_zh: 张成集可以是无限集
statement: The space of all polynomials is spanned by the infinite set of powers of t. Nothing in the definition of span forces S to be finite, even though each individual combination uses only finitely many terms.

anchors.quote: The space of all polynomials is spanned by the infinite set of polynomials $\{1, t, t^{2}, \ldots\}$ .

atomic_reason: One cardinality observation about S, kept separate from the finiteness of each combination.

name_en: The witnessing family must be finite
name_zh: 见证族必须是有限的
statement: The relation exhibiting dependence involves only finitely many elements of S, even when S is infinite. Dropping finiteness would require summing infinitely many terms, which is undefined in a linear space with no topology, so the definition would not even parse.

anchors.quote: is called dependent if there is a finite set of distinct elements in S

atomic_reason: A single condition on the cardinality of the witnessing family; it is one of the four independently variable parts of the definition.

name_en: The chosen elements must be distinct
name_zh: 所选元素必须互不相同
statement: The witnessing elements x_1 through x_k are required to be distinct. Drop this and every nonempty set becomes dependent: take x_1 = x_2 = x with c_1 = 1, c_2 = -1, giving a nonzero coefficient tuple summing to O.

anchors.quote: if there is a finite set of distinct elements in S, say $x_{1}, \ldots, x_{k}$

atomic_reason: A single injectivity condition on the indexing of the witnessing family; one of the four independently variable parts.

name_en: The coefficients must not all be zero
name_zh: 系数必须不全为零
statement: At least one c_i is required to be nonzero. Drop this clause and every nonempty set, in particular every singleton, becomes dependent, since the all-zero tuple always yields O and the notion would carry no information at all. The empty set is unaffected, because the witnessing family x_1, ..., x_k is understood to have k >= 1, so it has no witness either way.

anchors.quote: and corresponding set of scalars $c_{1}, \ldots, c_{k}$ , not all zero, such that

atomic_reason: A single nontriviality condition on the coefficient tuple; one of the four independently variable parts.

name_en: The linear combination must equal the zero element
name_zh: 线性组合必须等于零元
statement: The witnessing combination is required to equal O, the zero element of V. Replace O by an arbitrary target y and the condition stops describing dependence and instead describes membership of y in the span of S.
atomic_reason: A single equation naming the target of the combination; one of the four independently variable parts.

name_en: Dependence is witnessed by one explicit relation
name_zh: 相关性由一条显式关系见证
statement: Example 5 shows the practical shape of a dependence proof: exhibit a single identity with nonzero coefficients. The Pythagorean identity gives cos squared plus sin squared minus 1 equal to O, so those three functions are dependent.

anchors.quote: The Pythagorean identity shows that $u_{1} + u_{2} - u_{3} = O$ , so the three functions $u_{1}, u_{2}, u_{3}$ are dependent.

atomic_reason: A single worked instance of the existential definition; it has no proof structure beyond citing one identity.

name_en: A scalar multiple relation between two elements forces dependence
name_zh: 两元素成标量倍数关系即导致相关
statement: Example 2: if some element of S equals a scalar times another element of S, then S is dependent. This is the cheapest sufficient condition for dependence and needs only two elements of S.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 2. If one element in S is a scalar multiple of another, then S is dependent.

atomic_reason: A one-line sufficient condition whose proof is a single two-term relation.

name_en: Independence is a universal statement over all finite subfamilies and all coefficient tuples
name_zh: 独立性是对全部有限子族与全部系数组的全称陈述
statement: Negating the existential in the dependence definition turns independence into a claim about all choices of distinct elements of S and all scalar tuples. This is why an independence proof must handle an arbitrary relation rather than exhibit one.

anchors.quote: In this case, for all choices of distinct elements $x_{1},\ldots ,x_{k}$ in $S$ and scalars $c_{1},\ldots ,c_{k}$ ,

atomic_reason: One quantifier flip; it is the outermost logical shape of independence.

name_en: A vanishing combination forces every coefficient to vanish
name_zh: 组合为零迫使每个系数为零
statement: The working form of independence: if a finite combination of distinct elements of S equals O, then all the coefficients are zero. This implication is the statement every independence proof in the chapter actually verifies.

anchors.quote: \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} c _ {i} x _ {i} = O \quad i m p l i e s \quad c _ {1} = c _ {2} = \dots = c _ {k} = 0.

atomic_reason: A single implication with no internal case split; it is the operational core of the definition.

name_en: The empty set is independent
name_zh: 空集是独立的
statement: Example 4: with no elements available there is no finite family of distinct elements to witness dependence, so the empty set is independent by vacuity. This boundary case is what makes the zero space fit the basis machinery.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 4. The empty set is independent.

atomic_reason: A vacuous-truth boundary case about a single set; nothing smaller exists.

name_en: The definition applies to infinite sets as well
name_zh: 定义不限于有限集
statement: For finite S the definition agrees with the earlier one for V_n, but here S itself may be infinite while each witnessing relation stays finite. This separation of two finiteness questions is what lets Example 6 speak of an infinite independent set.

anchors.quote: However, the present definition is not restricted to finite sets.

atomic_reason: One scope statement about the domain of the definition; it has no decomposable interior.

name_en: Independence of an infinite set reduces to independence of its finite subsets
name_zh: 无限集的独立性归约为其有限子集的独立性
statement: To prove the infinite set of powers independent, Apostol proves that for each n the first n+1 powers are independent. This reduction works because every witnessing relation is finite, so no relation can involve more than finitely many members.

anchors.quote: The set $S = \{u_{0}, u_{1}, u_{2}, \ldots\}$ is independent. To prove this, it suffices to show that for each $n$ the $n + 1$ polynomials

atomic_reason: A single reduction move; its justification is exactly the finiteness clause already isolated as its own node.

name_en: In a function space the relation equals O means a pointwise identity
name_zh: 函数空间中等于零元意为逐点恒等
statement: When V is a space of real-valued functions, the zero element O is the function that vanishes everywhere, so a relation summing to O is an identity holding for every value of the variable. Example 6 exploits this by substituting t = 0 and then differentiating repeatedly; Example 7 exploits it by multiplying by e^{-a_M x} and letting x tend to +infinity.

anchors.quote: A relation of the form $\sum c_{k} u_{k} = O$ means that

atomic_reason: A single unpacking of what the symbol O denotes in one class of linear spaces; there is nothing smaller to isolate.

name_en: Independence of the powers of t by repeated differentiation at zero
name_zh: 用反复求导并在零点取值证明 t 的幂的独立性
statement: Example 6 extracts the coefficients one at a time: setting t = 0 gives c_0, differentiating once and setting t = 0 gives c_1, and repeating gives every c_k. The technique is analytic, not algebraic: it needs differentiability of polynomials and the fact that an identity in t may be differentiated.

anchors.quote: When $t = 0$ , this gives $c_0 = 0$ . Differentiating (15.1) and setting $t = 0$ , we find that $c_1 = 0$ . Repeating the process, we find that each coefficient $c_k$ is zero.

atomic_reason: One coefficient-extraction technique described as a single repeatable step; splitting per index k would just re-index the same step.

name_en: Hypothesis of Example 7: the exponents are distinct real numbers
name_zh: 例7的前提:指数是互不相同的实数
statement: Independence is asserted only for exponential functions whose exponents are pairwise distinct. If two exponents coincide the two functions are equal, hence dependent by the scalar-multiple criterion, so distinctness is not removable.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 7. If $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ are distinct real numbers, the $n$ exponential functions

atomic_reason: A single hypothesis clause on the parameter tuple; one condition, one failure mode.

name_en: Proof architecture: induction on n with a one-coefficient kill per level
name_zh: 证明架构:对 n 归纳,每层杀掉一个系数
statement: The architecture has three parts with a fixed dependency order: a base case n = 1 that needs nothing; an elimination step that picks the largest exponent a_M, normalizes by e^{-a_M x}, and takes x to +infinity to force c_M = 0; and a descent step that deletes the M-th term and calls the hypothesis on the remaining n - 1 functions. Only the elimination step uses the hypothesis that the exponents are distinct -- it is what makes a_k - a_M strictly negative for k not M -- while the recursion itself is independent of it, so the recursion depth equals the number of functions and each level kills exactly one coefficient.

anchors.quote: We can prove this by induction on $n$ . The result holds trivially when $n = 1$ . Therefore, assume it is true for $n - 1$ exponential functions and consider scalars

atomic_reason: Not atomic: it names a proof architecture whose base case, reduction step and appeal to the hypothesis are separate nodes below.

name_en: Base case: a single exponential function is independent
name_zh: 归纳起点:单个指数函数是独立的
statement: For n = 1 the claim is that c times e to the a x vanishing identically forces c = 0, which holds because the exponential function is never zero. Apostol calls this trivial and does not expand it.

anchors.quote: The result holds trivially when $n = 1$ .

atomic_reason: The minimal case of the induction; it consists of one substitution and one appeal to nonvanishing of the exponential.

name_en: Selecting the largest exponent
name_zh: 选取最大的指数
statement: The step picks a_M to be the largest of the n exponents. This uses the total ordering of the reals and the finiteness of the index set, so a maximum exists; the choice is what makes all the other exponents smaller by a strictly negative amount.

anchors.quote: Let $a_{M}$ be the largest of the n numbers $a_{1},\ldots ,a_{n}$ .

atomic_reason: One selection step justified by one order-theoretic fact; it has no substeps.

name_en: Multiplying the relation by the reciprocal of the largest exponential
name_zh: 用最大指数项的倒数乘整个关系
statement: Multiplying the relation through by e to the minus a_M x replaces each exponent a_k by the shifted exponent a_k minus a_M. The step is legitimate and reversible because the exponential function never vanishes, and it collapses the M-th term to the constant c_M.

anchors.quote: Multiplying both members of (15.2) by $e^{-a_M x}$ , we obtain

atomic_reason: A single reversible multiplication; the algebraic law and the nonvanishing fact it depends on are separate nodes.

name_en: Non-algebraic input: the exponential addition law
name_zh: 非代数输入:指数加法律
statement: Rewriting e to the a_k x times e to the minus a_M x as e to the (a_k minus a_M) x is a property of the exponential function, not of the linear space. Without it the multiplication would not simplify the relation at all.
atomic_reason: One functional identity imported from outside linear algebra; it is a single fact.

name_en: The shifted exponents are strictly negative off the maximal index
name_zh: 除最大指标外平移后的指数严格为负
statement: For every k different from M the number a_k minus a_M is negative. This is where the distinctness hypothesis is consumed: without distinctness a tie would give a shifted exponent equal to zero and the corresponding term would not decay.

anchors.quote: If $k \neq M$ , the number $a_k - a_M$ is negative.

atomic_reason: One sign determination for one family of differences; it is the smallest step that uses the hypothesis.

name_en: Non-algebraic input: a limit as x tends to infinity kills all but one term
name_zh: 非代数输入:令 x 趋于无穷的极限论证消去除一项外的全部项
statement: Letting x tend to plus infinity makes every term with a negative shifted exponent tend to zero, leaving c_M = 0. This is the decisive step and it is analytic: it uses limits and the decay of the exponential, notions absent from the linear space axioms.

anchors.quote: Therefore, when $x \to +\infty$ in Equation (15.3), each term with $k \neq M$ tends to zero and we find that $c_M = 0$ .

atomic_reason: A single limit evaluation producing a single conclusion c_M = 0.

name_en: Deleting the killed term and invoking the induction hypothesis
name_zh: 删去已被消去的项并调用归纳假设
statement: With c_M shown to be zero, the M-th term drops out and the remaining relation involves n-1 exponentials with distinct exponents, so the induction hypothesis kills the remaining coefficients. This is the step that closes the recursion.

anchors.quote: Deleting the $M$ th term from (15.2) and applying the induction hypothesis, we find that each of the remaining $n - 1$ coefficients $c_k$ is zero.

atomic_reason: One deletion plus one appeal to the hypothesis; the two are inseparable as a single closing move.

name_en: What the exponential proof does not use
name_zh: 指数函数独立性证明没有用到什么
statement: The argument uses ordering of the reals, the exponential addition law, nonvanishing of the exponential and one limit. It uses no inner product, no norm, no orthogonality, no differentiation and no dimension count, which is why it works in the space of all real-valued functions on the line.
origin_note: A negative claim about the proof, obtained by inspecting every step of Example 7 in 15.07. Not stated by Apostol.
atomic_reason: A single scoping claim about the proof's toolkit; it enumerates rather than decomposes.

name_en: Theorem 15.5 hypothesis: S is independent with exactly k elements
name_zh: 定理15.5的前提:S 独立且恰有 k 个元素
statement: The hypothesis fixes a count k and requires S to be independent. Independence is what makes k the sharp threshold: it is the reason the theorem speaks of k+1 rather than of some smaller number of elements.

anchors.quote: Let S be an independent set consisting of k elements in a linear space V

atomic_reason: One hypothesis clause pairing a cardinality with an independence requirement; neither part varies without changing the statement.

name_en: Theorem 15.5 conclusion: every set of k+1 elements of L(S) is dependent
name_zh: 定理15.5的结论:L(S) 中任意 k+1 个元素相关
statement: The conclusion is universally quantified over all sets of k+1 elements drawn from the span, not from V. Note that the k+1 elements need not lie in S; they need only be expressible as finite combinations of members of S.

anchors.quote: and let $L(S)$ be the subspace spanned by S. Then every set of $k + 1$ elements in $L(S)$ is dependent.

atomic_reason: One universally quantified conclusion; it has no independently variable clauses.

name_en: Theorem 15.5 is proved by delegation to Theorem 12.8
name_zh: 定理15.5的证明委派给定理12.8
statement: Apostol gives no new argument in 15.07. He observes that in V_n the statement is Theorem 12.8 and then argues that the old proof transfers. So the load-bearing wall of the dimension theory has no proof inside Chapter 15.

anchors.quote: When $V = V_{n}$ , Theorem 15.5 reduces to Theorem 12.8.

atomic_reason: A single delegation step. Its interior lies in Chapter 12, which is outside the sources assigned here, so it cannot be split further from 15.07 alone.

name_en: The transfer argument: the old proof used only the linear space axioms
name_zh: 迁移论证:旧证明只用到线性空间公理
statement: The justification for reusing the proof of Theorem 12.8 is an audit of that proof: it rests only on V_n being a linear space and on no other special property of V_n. This audit, not any new computation, is what makes Theorem 15.5 hold in arbitrary linear spaces.

anchors.quote: we find that it is based only on the fact that $V_{n}$ is a linear space and nc on any other special property of $V_{n}$ .

atomic_reason: One meta-level observation about a proof's dependencies; it is the smallest unit that can carry the generalization.

name_en: A basis must be independent
name_zh: 基必须是独立的
statement: The first of the two clauses defining a finite basis. Independence is what makes the representation of an element unique; drop it and the set may still span but the coefficients cease to be determined.

anchors.quote: A finite set S of elements in a linear space V is called a finite basis for V if S is independent and spans V.

atomic_reason: One of the two independently variable clauses of the definition; internally it just cites the independence definition.

name_en: A basis must span the space
name_zh: 基必须张成整个空间
statement: The second of the two clauses. Spanning is what makes the representation of an element exist at all; drop it and an independent set represents only the elements of its own span.

anchors.quote: is called a finite basis for V if S is independent and spans V

atomic_reason: One of the two independently variable clauses of the definition; internally it just cites the span definition.

name_en: The independence clause and the spanning clause are logically independent
name_zh: 独立性条款与张成条款彼此逻辑独立
statement: Neither clause implies the other. The set containing O, i, -i, j, -j and i+j spans V_2 without being independent, and a single nonzero vector of V_2 is independent without spanning V_2. So a basis is genuinely a conjunction of two separate requirements.
origin_note: The independence of the two clauses is not stated by Apostol; it is inferred from the spanning examples of 15.06 quoted in the anchor.
atomic_reason: A single non-implication claim in both directions; each direction is witnessed by one example.

name_en: Finiteness is part of the phrase finite basis
name_zh: 有限性是「有限基」一词的组成部分
statement: The definition speaks of a finite set S. Finiteness is not derived from independence or spanning; it is stipulated, and it is what makes the element count in Theorem 15.6 a well-defined integer.

anchors.quote: A finite set S of elements in a linear space V is called a finite basis for V

atomic_reason: A single cardinality stipulation; it is the third independently variable part of the definition.

name_en: Finite dimensionality means a finite basis exists
name_zh: 有限维即存在有限基
statement: V is finite dimensional if some finite basis for V exists. The definition is existential over bases, which is exactly why Theorem 15.6 is needed before a number can be attached to V.

anchors.quote: The space V is called finite dimensional if it has a finite basis, or if V consists of O alone.

atomic_reason: One existential clause over bases; nothing smaller remains.

name_en: The zero space is declared finite dimensional separately
name_zh: 零空间被单列宣告为有限维
statement: The clause or if V consists of O alone is a second disjunct, not a consequence of the first. Formally it is redundant: by Example 4 the empty set is independent, and by the convention of 15.06 it spans {O}, so the empty set already is a finite basis for the zero space. Apostol lists the case separately so that the definition need not lean on those two boundary conventions.

anchors.quote: or if V consists of O alone. Otherwise V is called infinite dimensional.
If S is empty, we define $L(S)$ to be $\{O\}$ , the set consisting of the zero element alone.

atomic_reason: A boundary-case stipulation covering one space; it cannot be subdivided.

name_en: Operational criterion: no finite set spans the space
name_zh: 可操作判据:没有有限集能张成该空间
statement: Example 4 shows the usable form of the criterion. The polynomials are infinite dimensional because although the infinite set of powers spans them, no finite set of polynomials does. The failure is located in spanning, not in independence.

anchors.quote: Although the infinite set $\{1, t, t^{2}, \ldots\}$ spans this space, no finite set of polynomials spans the space.

atomic_reason: One negative spanning condition; it is the minimal checkable form of the residual definition.

name_en: Operational criterion: for every n there exist n independent elements
name_zh: 可操作判据:对任意 n 都存在 n 个独立元
statement: Equivalently, V is infinite dimensional when for each n one can produce n independent elements of V. If V had a basis of k elements, Theorem 15.5 would make every k+1 elements dependent, contradicting the criterion at n = k+1.
origin_note: This positive criterion is not stated in 15.08; Apostol gives only the negative spanning form. Derived here from Theorem 15.5.
atomic_reason: One quantified criterion whose proof of equivalence is a single application of Theorem 15.5.

name_en: Theorem 15.6 hypothesis: V is finite dimensional
name_zh: 定理15.6的前提:V 是有限维的
statement: The equal-cardinality theorem is stated only for finite-dimensional V and compares only finite bases. It says nothing about infinite bases, which Apostol never introduces in this chapter.

anchors.quote: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional linear space. Then every finite basis for $V$ has the same number of elements.

atomic_reason: One hypothesis clause plus the scope restriction to finite bases; a single indivisible framing.

name_en: Applying Theorem 15.5 to S to bound sets of size k+1
name_zh: 对 S 应用定理15.5以界定 k+1 元集
statement: Because S is independent and spans V, Theorem 15.5 applies with L(S) equal to V and yields that every set of k+1 elements of V is dependent. Both clauses of the basis definition are consumed here: independence to satisfy the hypothesis, spanning to identify L(S) with V.

anchors.quote: Since S is independent and spans V, Theorem 15.5 tells us that every set of $k + 1$ elements in V is dependent.

atomic_reason: A single theorem application; its two hypothesis checks are already separate nodes.

name_en: Upgrading from exactly k+1 elements to more than k elements
name_zh: 从恰好 k+1 个元升级到多于 k 个元
statement: Theorem 15.5 speaks of k+1 elements, but the proof needs every set of more than k elements. The upgrade is silent in the text and rests on the fact that a set containing a dependent subset is dependent, which is Example 1 of 15.07.

anchors.quote: Therefore, every set of more than k elements in V is dependent.

atomic_reason: One monotonicity step; it is exactly one application of the superset lemma.

name_en: First inequality: m is at most k
name_zh: 第一个不等式:m 不超过 k
statement: T is independent, so T cannot have more than k elements, giving m at most k. Only the independence half of T being a basis is used at this point; its spanning property is not needed yet.

anchors.quote: Since T is an independent set, we must have $m \leq k$ .

atomic_reason: One contrapositive step yielding one inequality.

name_en: The symmetry step is where T being a spanning set is consumed
name_zh: 对称步骤正是用到 T 张成 V 的地方
statement: Interchanging S and T gives k at most m, but this reuse is legitimate only because T also spans V, so that Theorem 15.5 can be applied with T in the role of S. The phrase the same argument hides the second, and only, use of T being a spanning set.

anchors.quote: The same argument with S and T interchanged shows that $k \leq m$ .

atomic_reason: One symmetry appeal producing one inequality; the hidden hypothesis it needs is named in the statement.

name_en: Conclusion by antisymmetry of the order on the integers
name_zh: 由整数序的反对称性得出结论
statement: From m at most k and k at most m the equality k = m follows. The only input to this final step is the antisymmetry of the ordering of the integers; the two inequalities it consumes are each produced by Theorem 15.5, applied once in each direction.

anchors.quote: The same argument with S and T interchanged shows that $k \leq m$ . Therefore k = m.

atomic_reason: A single order-theoretic inference closing the proof.

name_en: Dimension is defined as the number of elements in a basis
name_zh: 维数定义为某个基的元素个数
statement: The definition attaches to V the integer n whenever V has a basis of n elements. As written, the integer is read off from one chosen basis, so the definition is a priori a property of the pair (space, basis).

anchors.quote: If a linear space V has a basis of n elements, the integer n is called the dimension of V.

atomic_reason: One assignment of an integer to a space; its legitimacy is a separate node.

name_en: Well-definedness of dimension rests on all bases having the same size
name_zh: 维数的良定义性依赖任两个基等势
statement: Reading n off from a chosen basis defines a function of V only because Theorem 15.6 makes n independent of the choice. Without Theorem 15.6 the phrase the dimension of V would not denote anything, so dimension does not hang on its definition alone but on the definition together with Theorem 15.6.

anchors.quote: Then every finite basis for $V$ has the same number of elements.

atomic_reason: One well-definedness obligation discharged by exactly one theorem.

name_en: The zero space is assigned dimension 0 by convention
name_zh: 零空间按约定赋维数 0
statement: Since the zero space has no basis of positive size, its dimension is fixed by a separate stipulation. Under the convention that the empty set is independent and spans the zero space, this stipulation is consistent with the general definition.

anchors.quote: If $V = \{O\}$ , we say V has dimension 0.

atomic_reason: A boundary-case stipulation for one space; nothing smaller exists.

name_en: The dimension of V_n is n, witnessed by the unit coordinate vectors
name_zh: V_n 的维数为 n,由单位坐标向量见证
statement: Example 1 computes a dimension the only way available: exhibit one basis and count it. The n unit coordinate vectors serve as the witness.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 1. The space $V_{n}$ has dimension $n$ . One basis is the set of $n$ unit coordinate vectors.

atomic_reason: One dimension computation by one exhibited basis.

name_en: The polynomials of degree at most n have dimension n+1
name_zh: 次数不超过 n 的多项式空间维数为 n+1
statement: Example 2 counts the basis of powers from the constant through the n-th power, giving n+1 elements. The off-by-one is a standing trap: the degree bound is n but the dimension is n+1.

anchors.quote: The space of all polynomials $p(t)$ of degree $\leq n$ has dimension $n + 1$ . One basis is the set of $n + 1$ polynomials

atomic_reason: One dimension computation by one exhibited basis.

name_en: The solution space of y'' - 2y' - 3y = 0 has dimension 2 (Example 3)
name_zh: 例3:方程 y'' - 2y' - 3y = 0 的解空间维数为 2
statement: Example 3 gives dimension 2 for the solution space of the single equation y'' - 2y' - 3y = 0, one basis being u_1(x) = e^{-x}, u_2(x) = e^{3x}. Apostol proves nothing here about second-order homogeneous equations in general. Verifying that this pair is independent is exactly Example 7 of 15.07 with the two distinct exponents -1 and 3.

anchors.quote: One basis consists of the two functions $u_1(x) = e^{-x}$ , $u_2(x) = e^{3x}$ .

atomic_reason: One dimension computation by one exhibited basis; the independence check is delegated to an existing node.

name_en: Theorem 15.7 hypothesis: V is finite dimensional of dimension n
name_zh: 定理15.7的前提:V 有限维且维数为 n
statement: Both parts are stated under a fixed dimension n. Part (b) is meaningless without it, since the number n in n independent elements refers to the dimension and to nothing else.

anchors.quote: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional linear space with $\dim V = n$ . Then we have the following:

atomic_reason: One hypothesis clause fixing one integer parameter.

name_en: Theorem 15.7(a): every independent set is contained in a basis
name_zh: 定理15.7(a):每个独立集都含于某个基中
statement: Part (a) asserts an extension property: an independent set, of any size up to n, sits inside some basis for V. The assertion is existential in the basis and says nothing about which basis or how to find it.

anchors.quote: (a) Any set of independent elements in $V$ is a subset of some basis for $V$ .

atomic_reason: One existential extension claim; its proof lies in Chapter 12 and is not available in the assigned sources.

name_en: Theorem 15.7(b): n independent elements already form a basis
name_zh: 定理15.7(b):n 个独立元已构成基
statement: Part (b) says that once the count reaches the dimension, independence alone forces spanning. This is the practical half of the theorem: it removes the obligation to check spanning whenever the count is right.

anchors.quote: (b) Any set of n independent elements is a basis for V.

atomic_reason: One implication converting a count plus independence into a basis.

name_en: Both parts of Theorem 15.7 are proved by delegation to Theorem 12.10
name_zh: 定理15.7两部分的证明都委派给定理12.10
statement: Apostol reproduces no argument: part (a) is said to be identical to part (b) of Theorem 12.10 and part (b) identical to part (c). So within Chapter 15 the proof of 15.7 is empty, and the only chapter-internal ingredient available is Theorem 15.5.

anchors.quote: The proof of (a) is identical to that of part (b) of Theorem 12.10. The proof of (b) is identical to that of part (c) of Theorem 12.10.

atomic_reason: A single delegation statement. Its interior lies in Chapter 12, outside the assigned sources, so it cannot be opened here.

name_en: In a space of dimension n every n+1 elements are dependent
name_zh: 在 n 维空间中任意 n+1 个元素必相关
statement: Applying Theorem 15.5 to a basis of V, whose span is V itself, gives that every set of n+1 elements of V is dependent. It is not part of the statement of Theorem 15.7; it is the consequence of Theorem 15.5 that the proof of 15.7(b) uses, and its whole proof is one instantiation of Theorem 15.5.

anchors.quote: Then every set of $k + 1$ elements in $L(S)$ is dependent.

origin_note: Apostol does not state this as a numbered result in Chapter 15; it is Theorem 15.5 instantiated at a basis. The anchor quotes the conclusion of Theorem 15.5 that is being instantiated.
atomic_reason: One instantiation of an existing theorem at one particular independent set.

name_en: Why n independent elements must span: adjoining an outside element breaks the count
name_zh: n 个独立元为何必然张成:添加界外元素会突破计数上界
statement: If n independent elements failed to span V, some element of V would lie outside their span; adjoining it would produce n+1 independent elements of V, contradicting the fact that every n+1 elements are dependent. The argument is a proof by contradiction whose contradiction point is a cardinality bound.
origin_note: Apostol delegates the proof of 15.7(b) to Theorem 12.10 and gives no argument in 15.08. This is the standard reconstruction from the chapter-internal ingredients only.
atomic_reason: Not atomic: it needs the separate lemma that adjoining an element outside the span preserves independence.

name_en: Lemma: adjoining an element outside the span keeps a set independent
name_zh: 引理:添加张成集之外的元素保持独立性
statement: If a set is independent and y is not in its span, then the set enlarged by y is still independent, because in any vanishing relation the coefficient of y must be zero, else y would be a combination of the others. This lemma is the engine of both the extension in part (a) and the contradiction in part (b).
origin_note: Not stated in 15.06 through 15.08. Recorded as model-origin because it is the missing link that the delegation to Theorem 12.10 conceals.
atomic_reason: One implication whose proof is a single case split on whether the new coefficient vanishes.

name_en: What the chain from 15.5 to 15.7 does not use
name_zh: 从15.5到15.7这条链没有用到什么
statement: Theorem 15.5, Theorem 15.6 and Theorem 15.7 use only the linear space axioms, the finiteness of the counts and the ordering of the integers. No inner product, norm, orthogonality, distance, coordinates or completeness appears, which is why all of 15.10 onward can be built on top of this layer rather than beside it.

anchors.quote: it is based only on the fact that $V_{n}$ is a linear space and nc on any other special property of $V_{n}$

origin_note: The scoping claim over all three theorems is inferred; the anchor is Apostol's own statement of it for the 15.5 ingredient only.
atomic_reason: A single negative scoping claim about a fixed set of three theorems.

name_en: An ordered basis adds an ordering that a basis as a set does not carry
name_zh: 有序基在基之上附加了集合本身不具备的次序
statement: A basis is a set and therefore unordered; an ordered basis is the basis together with a chosen enumeration, recorded as an n-tuple. The ordering is extra data, and permuting it gives a different ordered basis for the same basis.

anchors.quote: consider a basis whose elements $e_1, \ldots, e_n$ are taken in a given order. We denote such an ordered basis as an $n$ -tuple $(e_1, \ldots, e_n)$ .

atomic_reason: One added datum on top of an existing object; there is nothing smaller than the choice of an enumeration.

name_en: Existence of the expansion comes from the spanning clause
name_zh: 展开式的存在性来自张成条款
statement: That every element of V can be written as a combination of the basis elements is the spanning half of the basis definition, nothing more. Independence plays no role in the existence of the expansion.

anchors.quote: If $x \in V$ , we can express $x$ as a linear combination of these basis elements:

atomic_reason: One existence claim traced to one clause of one definition.

name_en: The component tuple depends on the ordering, not only on the basis set
name_zh: 分量组依赖于次序,而不仅依赖于基这个集合
statement: Because the components are recorded as an n-tuple indexed in the given order, permuting the ordered basis permutes the components of every element. This is the sole reason Apostol introduces ordered bases before components.

anchors.quote: are called the components of x relative to the ordered basis $(e_{1},\ldots,e_{n})$ .

origin_note: The permutation observation is not spelled out by Apostol; it is read off from the n-tuple notation quoted in the anchor.
atomic_reason: One dependence claim on one piece of data.

name_en: Uniqueness proof step 2: subtract to obtain a vanishing relation
name_zh: 唯一性证明第二步:相减得到一个为零的关系
statement: Subtracting the two expansions yields a combination of the basis elements with coefficients c_i minus d_i equal to O. This is the move that converts a uniqueness question into an independence question, and it uses only the linear space axioms.

anchors.quote: then by subtraction from (15.4), we find that $\sum_{i=1}^{n}(c_{i}-d_{i})e_{i}=O$ .

atomic_reason: One algebraic subtraction producing one relation.

name_en: Uniqueness proof step 3: independence forces the differences to vanish
name_zh: 唯一性证明第三步:独立性迫使差为零
statement: Since the basis elements are independent, the vanishing relation forces every c_i minus d_i to be zero, so the two coefficient tuples coincide. Uniqueness therefore consumes only the independence clause of the basis definition, while existence consumed only the spanning clause.

anchors.quote: But since the basis elements are independent, this implies $c_{i}=d_{i}$ for each i

atomic_reason: One application of the independence definition to one relation.

name_en: Conclusion: the coefficient tuple is uniquely determined by x
name_zh: 结论:系数组由 x 唯一确定
statement: The two tuples being equal, the expansion coefficients form an n-tuple determined by x alone once the ordered basis is fixed. This is what licenses treating components as a function of x.

anchors.quote: The coefficients in this equation determine an n-tuple of numbers $(c_{1},\ldots,c_{n})$ that is uniquely determined by x.

atomic_reason: One closing statement of well-definedness.
